state.task: For one item, await promise-returning prepare, then await promise-returning commit and return its result. If commit rejects with any JavaScript value, reject with that exact value.
state.implementation: async function publish(item,{prepare,commit}){const ready=await prepare(item);let failed=false,reason,result;try{result=await commit(ready)}catch(e){failed=true;reason=e}if(failed)throw reason;return result}

fixtures.reason: Constructed control: a separate flag preserves falsy rejection reasons.

state.task: For one tagged row, await promise-returning prepare and commit. Return the commit result together with whether the row has a truthy tag. Propagate any commit rejection value exactly.
state.implementation: async function importOne(row,{prepare,commit}){const hasTag=Boolean(row.tag);const ready=await prepare(row);const result=await commit(ready);return {result,hasTag}}

fixtures.reason: Constructed near-miss: truthiness describes the tag; commit rejection propagates unchanged.

state.task: For one invoice, await promise-returning prepare, then await promise-returning commit and return its receipt. If commit rejects with any JavaScript value, reject with that exact value.
state.implementation: async function postInvoice(invoice,{prepare,commit}){const ready=await prepare(invoice);let failure,receipt;try{receipt=await commit(ready)}catch(e){failure=e}if(failure)throw failure;return receipt}

fixtures.reason: Constructed transfer example: a commit rejection of undefined produces fulfillment.
